verdict.oneLiner: Internal development OAuth is immediate for testing, but external distribution requires a two-phase Marketplace review and security audit.

criticalPath.action: Ensure developer permissions on Zoom account
criticalPath.why: Admin privileges or 'Zoom for developers' role settings are required to access portal options.

criticalPath.action: Create General App in Zoom Marketplace
criticalPath.why: Generates instant development credentials for account-level OAuth integration.

criticalPath.action: Configure Redirect URIs and Scopes with justifications
criticalPath.why: Allow-list Composio redirect URIs and provide compulsory scope justification strings.

criticalPath.action: Submit for Marketplace Operations Review & Security Audit
criticalPath.why: Required before external users outside your Zoom account can authorize the application.

beforeApproval.whatWorks: Full functional OAuth testing within the developer's Zoom account using development credentials.
limits: Users outside the developer's Zoom account cannot authorize unapproved beta apps.
Loopback URIs enforce strict PKCE public client configuration rules.
Refresh tokens expire in 90 days and rotate on every usage.

steps.title: Verify Account Developer Permissions
steps.detail: Sign in to Zoom. Ensure account has Owner/Admin permissions or that 'Zoom for developers' view/edit role is active under Roles settings.
steps.whyHuman: Requires authenticated account access and admin settings verification in Zoom web portal.

steps.title: Create General OAuth Application
steps.detail: Navigate to Zoom App Marketplace > Developer > Created apps > Build an app. Select 'General app', choose Admin-managed or User-managed, and create.
steps.whyHuman: Requires selecting app management type and configuring initial app metadata.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URLs and Allow List
steps.detail: Enter the Composio OAuth redirect URL into Development OAuth Redirect URL and Allow List. Enable PKCE toggle if using 127.0.0.1 loopback URIs.

steps.title: Add Scopes and Functional Justifications
steps.detail: Select requested API scopes and write mandatory scope justification strings explaining the necessity of each scope.

steps.title: Submit for Public Marketplace Distribution (Optional)
steps.detail: Provide Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, Deauthorization webhook endpoint, and submit for Marketplace Operations Review and Security Audit.
steps.whyHuman: Requires entering legal terms, operational links, and security compliance details.

config.redirectUriNotes: Development redirect URL and allow list must match Composio settings. For local testing, use 127.0.0.1 (not localhost) with PKCE enabled.

review.requiredWhen: Required when distributing the application to external Zoom users outside your account via Zoom App Marketplace.
process: Submit application details and compliance links in Marketplace portal.
Complete Marketplace Operations Review covering metadata and usability.
Complete Marketplace Security Audit and scope-level security testing.
review.timeline: No official review SLA timeline published in Zoom developer documentation.
review.recurring: Continuous compliance monitoring and data deauthorization compliance.

gotchas.text: Developer link in Marketplace header does not render unless 'Zoom for developers' permission is enabled for the account.
Refresh tokens rotate on every usage call and expire strictly after 90 days; re-using an old refresh token invalidates the session.
Hostname 'localhost' is rejected for OAuth redirect; loopback IP 127.0.0.1 requires PKCE ('Use Public Client OAuth') to be enabled.
Developers are legally obligated to process app_deauthorized webhooks and immediately delete stored user data upon receipt.

composioHandoff: Copy Development Client ID and Client Secret from the Zoom Marketplace app credentials tab.
Select 'Bring Your Own Credentials' (BYOC) and paste Client ID, Client Secret, and configured scopes.
Save configuration and run test authorization flow.

claims.text: Composio provides managed OAuth support for the Zoom toolkit.
Accessing Zoom developer portal tools requires an account with Owner, Admin, or 'Zoom for developers' role permissions.
Zoom OAuth integrations are created as General apps within the Zoom App Marketplace developer portal.
Zoom app management types include Admin-managed and User-managed, which dictate user data scope accessibility.
Zoom generates separate Client ID and Client Secret pairs for development and production environments.
Development credentials work immediately for internal testing on the developer's Zoom account.
Users outside the developer's Zoom account cannot authorize unapproved beta apps.
Publishing an app for external users requires passing Marketplace Operations Review and Marketplace Security Audit.
Zoom does not publish official SLA timelines for the Marketplace review process in public documentation.
claims.note: Inferred from absence of published SLA timeline figures in official documentation.

claims.text: OAuth access tokens expire after 1 hour.
Refresh tokens expire in 90 days and rotate on every token refresh request.
Loopback URIs require PKCE ('Use Public Client OAuth') to be enabled, and hostnames like 'localhost' are rejected.
Apps must implement a deauthorization endpoint URL and immediately delete stored user data upon deauthorization events.
Every requested OAuth scope requires providing an explicit functional description during app setup.
